one_liner: Senior all-source intelligence analyst at DFC who researches classified and unclassified threats, writes intelligence products, and briefs senior leaders on counterintelligence risks.
fit_summary: The posting is open to the public, but it requires one year of GS-12-equivalent experience as a multi-source intelligence analyst with working knowledge of the national intelligence community. Nothing on file shows Daniel has done intelligence analysis. Daniel's IEM emergency-management consulting and policy knowledge are related but are unlikely to meet all three specialized-experience elements unless Daniel did actual threat or intelligence analysis there.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens) and federal transition candidates; a separate Merit Promotion announcement (27-SID-ST-13099059-CH) is for status candidates, so Daniel should use this public one.

Requires one year of specialized experience at the GS-12 level covering ALL three elements: multi-source intelligence analysis and production, advanced analytical methods applied to multiple sources, and working knowledge of the national intelligence community's structure and operations.
Education cannot substitute at GS-13; no degree is required.
The position requires Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) access, which means a Top Secret background investigation and possibly a polygraph.
The application window is very short: October 29 to November 4, 2026.
strategy: Before applying, honestly check whether your IEM work involved threat or hazard assessment, situational-awareness reporting, or analysis of multiple information sources for government clients. Apply only if you can truthfully document all three specialized-experience elements.

If you did that kind of work, frame it in analytic terms: the sources you synthesized (federal, state, and open-source reporting), the methods you used, the products you wrote, and who you briefed. Include hours per week and exact dates on a two-page resume.
Preview the questionnaire at apply.usastaffing.gov/ViewQuestionnaire/13099300 before starting, and answer conservatively, because overstating can get you removed from consideration.
State any existing clearance or prior background investigation prominently, since SCI eligibility weighs heavily.
Submit early given the six-day window, and save a resume version so you can reuse it for similar postings.

More realistically, target GS-9/11 emergency management, program analyst, or legislative/policy roles (FEMA, DHS, Virginia VDEM, Prince William County) where your IEM and policy background fits directly.
resume_bullets: Analyzed [type of information, e.g., federal, state, and open-source reporting] from [number] sources to produce [product type] for [government client], informing [decision or outcome], [hours/week], [dates].
Briefed [audience, e.g., senior state/federal officials or interagency partners] on [hazard/threat topic], clearly distinguishing confirmed facts from assessments and identifying [information gaps].
Applied [analytic method, e.g., risk assessment, trend/pattern analysis] to [dataset or scenario] to support [preparedness/recovery planning] for [client].
interview_questions: Walk us through an analytic product you wrote: what sources did you use, and how did you communicate confidence and gaps?
How would you handle conflicting reporting from two credible sources?
Describe your understanding of the Intelligence Community's structure and how DFC might interact with it.
Tell us about briefing a senior leader who disagreed with your assessment.
watch_outs: The specialized experience is narrow (an intelligence-analyst background), and nothing on file shows Daniel has it. Applying without it will likely end at the eligibility screen.
SCI clearance processing is lengthy and may involve a polygraph.
The six-day application window closes November 4, 2026.
The job is in-office in Washington, DC with telework eligibility, so expect a commute from Manassas.
